title: Grandmother's tea
intro: Tom is a guest at the house of Mina's grandmother, and he learns two things every visitor to Iran needs to know: how to drink tea with a sugar cube, and how to say 'no, thank you' – which in Iran is never the end of the conversation. The story uses the present tense, polite phrases like بفرمایید and دست شما درد نکند, and gives you a first taste of تعارف (ta'ārof), the Persian art of politeness.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.fa: او به خانه‌ی مادربزرگ مینا می‌رود.
sentences.r: u be khāne-ye mādar-bozorg-e Minā mi-ravad.
sentences.en: He goes to the house of Mina's grandmother.
sentences.faV: او به خانه‌یِ مادَربُزُرگِ مینا می‌رَوَد.

sentences.en: The tea is in small glasses.
The tea is a lovely colour.
Grandmother says: "Please, have some, Tom dear!"

sentences.fa: تام قند را در استکان می‌گذارد.
sentences.r: Tām ghand rā dar estekān mi-gozārad.
sentences.en: Tom puts the sugar cube in his glass.
sentences.faV: تام قَند را دَر اِستِکان می‌گُذارَد.

sentences.fa: مینا می‌خندد و می‌گوید: «نه، تام! قند در دهان!»
sentences.r: Minā mi-khandad o mi-guyad: «na, Tām! ghand dar dahān!»
sentences.en: Mina laughs and says: "No, Tom! The sugar goes in your mouth!"
sentences.faV: مینا می‌خَندَد و می‌گویَد: «نه، تام! قَند دَر دَهان!»

sentences.fa: تام یک قند در دهان می‌گذارد و چای می‌خورد.
sentences.r: Tām yek ghand dar dahān mi-gozārad o chāy mi-khorad.
sentences.en: Tom puts a sugar cube in his mouth and drinks his tea.
sentences.faV: تام یِک قَند دَر دَهان می‌گُذارَد و چای می‌خورَد.

sentences.fa: تام می‌گوید: «نه، ممنون. دست شما درد نکند.»
sentences.r: Tām mi-guyad: «na, mamnun. dast-e shomā dard na-konad.»
sentences.en: Tom says: "No, thank you. Thank you for your trouble."
sentences.lit: No, thanks. May your hand not hurt.
sentences.faV: تام می‌گویَد: «نه، مَمنون. دَستِ شُما دَرد نَکُنَد.»

sentences.fa: مادربزرگ می‌گوید: «تعارف نکن، پسرم! نوش جان!»
sentences.r: mādar-bozorg mi-guyad: «ta'ārof na-kon, pesar-am! nush-e jān!»
sentences.en: Grandmother says: "Don't stand on ceremony, my boy! Enjoy it!"
sentences.faV: مادَربُزُرگ می‌گویَد: «تَعارُف نَکُن، پِسَرَم! نوشِ جان!»

sentences.fa: تام این چای را هم می‌خورد.
sentences.r: Tām in chāy rā ham mi-khorad.
sentences.faV: تام این چای را هَم می‌خورَد.

vocab.en: please (have some / go ahead / come in)
polite ritual of offering and refusing
my son; my boy (a friendly way to address a young man)

questions.q: What does Tom do first with the sugar cube?
options: he puts it in his glass
he puts it in his mouth

questions.q: Where, says Mina, does the sugar cube go?
What does Grandmother say when Tom says 'no, thank you'?

after: In many Iranian homes tea is still made in a samovar and served in small glasses (استکان) on a tray. Many people do not stir sugar into their tea: they hold a sugar cube (قند) in the mouth – or dip it in the tea first – and drink through it. Good tea is خوش‌رنگ, 'of a lovely colour': deep, clear red. The end of the story is pure ta'ārof: the guest politely refuses, the host insists with تعارف نکن 'don't stand on ceremony', and the guest gives in. Saying 'no' once is just being polite. دست شما درد نکند, literally 'may your hand not hurt', thanks someone for the trouble they took; نوش جان, 'may it nourish your soul', is what you say to someone who is eating or drinking; and جان after a name, as in تام جان, means 'dear'.
